text.p: The following stories were reported in Lithuanian newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Centre Union does not intend to withdraw its construction and urban planning and environment protection ministers from the cabinet but has appointed party supervisors to them.
- The German ministry of justice refused to extradite a 72-year-old years old former KGB officer Julius Slavinas indicted of genocide.
- Lithuania's Litimpeks bank said its losses in the first quarter of 1997 were 1.9 million litas.
- World Bank economist Marcelo Giugale said the finance ministry has little experience in privatising big state-run banks and suggested World Bank experts support.
- Chemical firm Jonavos Achema intends to acquire 1,000 shares with a 100 litas face value in the new 188.7 million litas share issue of Butinges oil terminal.
- Parliament chairman Vytautas Landsbergis said he would decide whether to take part in the presidential elections "without a long delay".

- A fire broke out in the left tire of a JAK 42B aircraft of Lithuanian Airlines on Sunday, 15 minutes after it landed in Vilnius airport after the flight from Moscow. The passengers had left the airport before the accident.
- The interior ministry plans to reform the border control system and impose order in the area with Belarus.

- Utenos Beverages decided to solve the dispute with the government over the state's stake in the company in the court. It will will have to decide whether the company owes the state 5 million litas or 164 litas.
